subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: What Control UI trust model should browser-login handoff use before implementation?
rationale: The feature would expose authenticated browser state and control actions through the operator UI, and automation cannot safely choose the UX, authorization, redaction, and core-versus-plugin ownership boundary.

options.title: Read-only-first handoff panel
options.body: Implement a browser-plugin or approved first-party panel that shows status, profile, tabs, and diagnostics first, with explicit user steps for focus, navigation, clicks, credential entry, and resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Defer browser-specific UI until maintainers land the generic plugin entry-point contract, then build the browser panel as a plugin-owned surface under that security model.

options.title: Defer the panel
options.body: Keep CLI/RPC browser management as the supported path until remote browser handoff becomes an explicitly prioritized product area.

recommendation.title: Read-only-first handoff panel
recommendation.body: Implement a browser-plugin or approved first-party panel that shows status, profile, tabs, and diagnostics first, with explicit user steps for focus, navigation, clicks, credential entry, and resume.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete supplied the canonical acceptance criteria in the issue discussion and also appears in recent adjacent Control UI history.
